svg.text: Longitudinal section through the cook bore, drawn 1:1 from the parametric CAD (scripts/build_model.py — the source of truth). One cell = a fixed heated tube bored through a wall, with a single piston.
Piston shown in the CHARGE pose (retracted 60 mm, cook chamber open). Its working poses — charge · cook · present · await-collect · clean — are in the cycle strip at right.
The piston face is simultaneously the flush public wall, the upper cook platen, the ejector, and the surface that parks in the sterilize zone. That is the whole machine (ADR-0001).
dry = no wet surface to sanitize

g.text: A–A (cook bore, through a scraper lip)
piston Ø160
bore Ø164 · wall 8 · running clearance 2 (mm)
ROUND: no corners, no seams — the scraper lip
wipes the whole perimeter on every stroke
B–B (sterilize zone, piston stowed)
steam / hot-water ring surrounds the stowed face
both food-contact surfaces cleaned in one place,
sealed away from the public side (ADR-0010)

svg.text: THE CYCLE — one serving, one chamber, one transfer

g.text: 1 · CHARGE
Piston retracts 60 mm. A metered dry blend drops from the
sealed hoppers into the open chamber. Surfaces now dirty.
2 · HYDRATE
Water + oil are injected as jets that do the mixing. No blade,
no mixer bowl — nothing extra to clean (ADR-0006).
3 · COOK
The piston presses the dough to 8 mm between two 230 °C
platens — the die end and the piston face. Both sides at once.
⚠ Drawn pressed-up, but nothing decides that — see flag 2 below.
4 · PRESENT — gated, never automatic
Only if SF1 proves the kill-step AND SF7 proves the batch is not
stale AND SF2 proved the surfaces clean. The die shears the rim
free. Any doubt ⇒ waste, not a person.
taken ⇒ served
not taken ⇒ waste
5 · AWAIT COLLECT (SF8, ADR-0018)
Presented is not served. The batch is held out until the face
sensor sees it GONE — a loaded→empty transition, never a level,
so a stuck sensor cannot invent a serving. Nobody comes within
120 s ⇒ withdraw, condemn, divert. This also bounds how long
the mouth stays open (H6).
6 · CLEAN
The face parks deep in the sealed sterilize zone: scrape (the lips
wiped the bore on the way past), steam, reused bake heat, dry.
Verified clean, or re-clean; three failures ⇒ lockout.

svg.text: MOUTH DETAIL — what ADR-0017 is actually about
A and B look at the wall from the street (~1:1). C is the die corner at 8:1. All drawn as the CAD actually is, not as the hazard register assumes.

g.text: A · SEALED (piston flush at X=0)
piston face
What H6's mitigation assumes: "mouth flush +
sealed except during present". True in IDLE and
at the end of the present stroke. Only there.
B · OPEN (piston retracted 60 mm)
open Ø156 hole
into a 230 °C chamber
What the CAD actually does through CHARGE and
HYDRATE — and, per ADR-0017, for the whole
~90 s bake. On a public street.
C · die corner, 8:1 — the whole "hot bore-end platen" (ADR-0007)
open to the
street
CookBarrel — wall 8
bore Ø164
MouthDie
dough disc
2 mm
of contact
ledge 4
Why the two halves are one decision
ADR-0007 bakes the disc by conduction between two heated
platens: the piston face, and "the heated bore-end/die".
Section C is what that second platen actually is.
The ledge between die ID Ø156 and bore ID Ø164 is 4 mm wide
radially — but the Ø160 disc overlaps the die by only 2 mm, so
the hot ring it can actually touch is 2 mm. Everything inside
Ø156 faces the open mouth, not metal.
A 2 mm contact ring cannot conduction-bake a Ø160 disc. So the
machine has no working lower platen AND no closure for the
mouth. Whatever closes the mouth probably has to BE the
platen — which is why ADR-0017 treats these as one decision,
not two. Its three options are in DECISIONS.md.
(ADR-0017 calls the ledge "2 mm". The ledge is 4 mm; the
contact is 2 mm. Its conclusion is unchanged.)

svg.text: Key dims (mm): flatbread Ø160 × 8 · bore Ø164 · piston Ø160 · wall 8 · running clearance 2 (2 scraper lips bridge it) · barrel 330 · piston 120 · charge depth 60 · sterilize stow 150 · stroke 210 · die 10 thk, Ø156 bore · platens 230 °C

Drawn 1:1 from scripts/build_model.py (mouth detail as noted). Scraper lips are shown exaggerated for legibility (true lip: 2 mm radial × 4 mm axial). Hoppers, waste chute and service plant are space-claim envelopes, not detailed.
FLAG 1 — the mouth is not sealed during the bake (ADR-0017, OPEN; blocks freezing the bore). The mouth die is a Ø156 ring and ADR-0001 rules out a separate door, so while
the piston is retracted the mouth is an open hole into the hot chamber (view B). That contradicts hazard H6, whose stated mitigation is "mouth flush + sealed except during present" —
a stated mitigation the geometry does not deliver, which is a worse class of problem than an unimplemented one. The CAD also gives no workable lower platen at that end (section C).
FLAG 2 — there is no PRESS step anywhere, so "where is the piston during the bake?" is undecided. Three artefacts disagree: build_model.py calls chargeDepth "the piston
retract that opens the charge/cook chamber" (60 mm open); ADR-0007 presses the dough to 8 mm between two platens; the twin runs CHARGE → HYDRATE → COOK without moving the piston
at all, and cycle panel 3 draws the bake already pressed up. Not cosmetic: if the press happens BEFORE the bake, the dough disc plugs the die and the exposure window is a few seconds
rather than ~90 s — which is most of ADR-0017's option 4, for free. Found while drawing this sheet. Nothing in the repo currently decides it.

g.text: 1 · CookBarrel — the fixed heated bore
A stationary tube through the wall, open at both ends: the
mouth at X=0, the service side at X=330. Its far end is the
lower cook platen. Round, so there is no corner to harbour
residue and nothing the scraper cannot reach.
2 · Piston — the ONE moving part
Its face is four things at once: the flush public wall when
closed, the upper cook platen, the ejector that delivers the
bread, and the surface that parks in the sterilize zone. One
heated moving part means one thing to clean, one to fail.
3 · ScraperSeals (SF3) — 2 lip rings
Compliant lips on the piston perimeter that bridge the 2 mm
running gap. They squeegee the full bore on every stroke and
separate the public side from the sealed service side.
4 · MouthDie — peeler + hard stop
Fixed hardened ring, proud of the wall. Its Ø156 bore is
smaller than the Ø160 piston, so it shears the bread rim free
on ejection and mechanically stops the piston at flush.
9 · DryStorage (SF6) — sealed hoppers
Everything upstream of the bore stays DRY: flour, legume,
salt, oil. A dry surface does not grow anything, so it never
needs sanitizing — the cheapest hygiene there is (ADR-0012).
5 · HydrationRing — jets, not a blade
Injects water + oil hard enough to do the mixing. Deleting the
mixer deletes a bowl, a shaft, a seal and a cleaning problem.
6 · SterilizeRing / 7 · HotAirKnife (SF2)
Steam and hot water sanitize the stowed piston face and the
bore around it, reusing bake heat; the air knife then dries
both. No per-cycle chemical to leave a residue on food.
8 · WasteChute — the divert path
Where a batch goes when it cannot be proven safe. It is a
real, physical branch: there is no code path from a failed
check to the mouth.
10 · ServicePlant · 11 · Beacon · 12 · Probes
Back-of-house drive, heaters, steam generator and dosers. The
beacon is the only public control surface — no buttons, no
handles. SF1's probes read the dough core and crust.

svg.text: SAFETY FUNCTIONS — what must be true to serve

g.text: SF1 · Cook lethality (primary)
An accumulated F-value, not a set-point: F₇₀ ≥ 13.9 equivalent
seconds = 7-log Salmonella. Four diverse channels, all must
agree; a fault reads "not cooked" (ADR-0009 / 0015).
SF2 · Surface sanitation (primary)
Proven clean since the last serving, or the line does not run.
SF3 · Contamination barrier
The scraper lips, separating public side from service side.
SF4 · Burn + pinch guard
Abort the present stroke rather than push through a hand or
hand over a scalding surface.
SF5 · Signalling + soft motion
Status beacon and a speed-limited final approach. Defence in
depth only — never relied on as a primary safeguard.
SF6 · Ingredient integrity
A wet or spoiled hopper refuses to charge.
SF7 · Bake→serve hold (primary)
Spores survive the bake and their toxin is heat-stable, so this
one is controlled by TIME: a batch held too long below 60 °C
is waste, not food (ADR-0016).
SF8 · Collection proof
A serving is not served until someone TAKES it — proven as a
loaded→empty transition, never a level, so a stuck sensor fails
to waste. An uncollected batch is withdrawn (ADR-0018).
